sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: The title page and introduction of a 1952 Bulletin of the World Health Organization article (in French) on dried smallpox vaccine, describing preparation of Otten's vaccine at the Pasteur Institute in Bandung, Indonesia. It explains that a heat-stable dried vaccine is needed for worldwide shipment and that over 26 million doses of Otten's vaccine were supplied in 1949.

sections.title: APEROU HISTORIQUE

summary.text: Gives a historical overview, in French, of preserving smallpox vaccine by drying, from early variolation with dried scabs and Jenner's dried vaccine on threads to nineteenth-century use of ivory points. It reviews successive drying techniques and reported storage times, moving on to vacuum and freeze-drying methods developed by various researchers in the twentieth century. The section ends with improvements such as purified dried vaccines prepared with antiseptics or tyrothricin.

sections.title: LE VACCIN SEC D'OTTEN ET SA PRaPARATION

summary.text: Describes the qualities of Otten's dried smallpox vaccine, stressing that it keeps its potency for years whatever the climate and can be produced cheaply in large quantities and stockpiled. It then sets out the preparation technique at the Bandung institute, covering the vaccine strain and its maintenance in buffalo, harvesting of pulp, drying, filling of ampoules and quality control. Results of tests on old stored batches show that most ampoules from the late 1920s remained virulent.

sections.title: RgSULTATS DE PRIMO-VACCINATIONS EFFECTUgES AVEC UN

summary.text: Presents results of primary vaccinations with 18-year-old dried vaccine, showing that several batches still produced reactions in most children, and begins a section on large-scale production in Indonesia. It notes that output was increased sharply during a major smallpox epidemic, while normal annual use is about 10 million doses.

sections.title: NOMBRE DES DISTRICTS AYANT UTILIS9 LE VACCIN SEC ET

summary.text: Tabulates the number of districts using the dried vaccine and doses delivered from 1931 to 1941, rising from 147,000 to about 800,000. It states that the vaccine is no more costly to make than glycerinated vaccine and then explains how vaccinators should reconstitute and use it, including how long suspensions may be kept at room temperature or in a refrigerator.

sections.title: SUMMARY

summary.text: The English and French summaries of the dried smallpox vaccine article, recounting the growth of Otten's vaccine use in Indonesia and the adaptation of the vaccine strain to buffalo. They outline how pulp is ground, dried under vacuum, powdered and sealed in ampoules, and how purity, virulence and antigenic potency are tested. The summaries report that the vaccine remained effective after 18 years of storage, and the block closes with the article's reference list.

sections.extract: RE2SUMEJ A dried smallpox vaccine has the ad- vantages that it can be prepared on a large scale, kept, and transported to all parts of the world without losing its potency. The dried vaccine made by Otten's method at the Institute Pasteur, Bandoeng, has been used in Indonesia since 1931 for vaccinat- ing the local population.
